title: Reranker model
subtitle: A cross-encoder reranker sits behind my hybrid retrieval, on a seam that tells load from breakage.
lede: The reranker is the published model, used without training or tuning; the engineering is in where it sits and how it fails. FAFOHive serves search to many agents at once, and the most expensive step in a search is the cross-encoder that reorders the candidates. the reranker model is that cross-encoder: it rescores the merged results of lexical and dense retrieval for code, reference and observation search. It runs as a local HTTP service. The call stays in process, with no queue hop between search and rerank, so its latency budget is predictable. The retrieval design is on Hybrid retrieval.
quote: When the reranker saturates, search quality degrades and search availability does not.
evidence: Cross-encoder reranking: a published reranker rescoring merged lexical and dense results for code, reference and observation search, called in process with no queue hop.
Capacity engineering for model endpoints: the reranker client wrapped in a bounded-endpoint primitive that sorts every failure into busy or broken, with separate counters.
author: Corey James
